history.dynasty: Early Cholas, with major contributions from Pandyas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara and Nayaks
history.period: Origins in antiquity; major construction 9th-17th centuries CE
history.summary: The Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam is the foremost and first of the 108 Divya Desams, glorified in the Divya Prabandha of the 6th-9th century Alvar saints, and is widely listed as the largest functioning Hindu temple complex in the world: 156 acres, seven concentric prakarams (outermost ~2.6 km), 21 sculpted gopurams, 50 sub-shrines and 9 temple tanks. The Rajagopuram rises ~236-237 ft (72 m) in eleven tiers — among Asia's tallest temple towers — above the gold-domed sanctum (Sri Vimanam) housing the reclining Ranganatha. On Srirangam island between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers; administration streamlined by the philosopher-saint Ramanuja. name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
town_description: Srirangam is a temple town on an island between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers, ~7-9 km north of Tiruchirappalli city. It is one of the foremost Vaishnavite pilgrimage centres in India, whose outer prakarams function as a living temple-town with streets, markets, lodges and multilingual guides.

travel.railway: Tiruchirappalli Junction ~7-9 km; Srirangam station (SRGM) close by (verify)
travel.road: Srirangam island is ~7 km north of Trichy city; well connected by bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi

visitor_information.best_time: October-March (pleasant weather, 15-25C); early morning 6-9 AM or evening 6-9 PM for peaceful darshan. Vaikunta Ekadasi (December-January) is the peak festival — spectacular but very crowded
